summary: Added an in-app Settings page to the myseliasan control plane, giving it its first self-service config editor (mymatasan already had one). A new Settings nav item under the System group (superadmin-only in both the nav gate and the API) exposes a SAFE SUBSET of config.json for read/edit: localAuth, sso, pairing, security (JWT secret, allowed origins, TLS paths, CSP, rate-limit tiers), storage (file storage/cleanup, cache/Redis), and logging (app/API log retention, Prometheus telemetry) -- db, server, and bootstrap stay file-only since a bad value there could take the app offline. Because the shared apphost reads these infra blocks only once at boot, PUT /api/settings/{section} validates and writes the change into both the live in-memory config and a surgical, order-preserving patch of config.json (untouched blocks keep their exact original bytes), then reports needsRestart; the page shows a persistent restart banner wired to a new POST /api/system/restart (superadmin-gated, relaunches the process via the existing apphost Restarter and polls health until the new process answers). A per-section Restore defaults (POST /api/settings/{section}/reset) reverts to a one-time first-run snapshot captured automatically and stored in the control-plane DB, encrypted via the existing fleet cipher when encryption at rest is enabled. Secret fields (local admin password, SSO client secret, JWT secret, Redis password) are never sent to the browser -- masked plus a "set" flag, and a blank field on save keeps the current value. The feature grew substantially beyond the initial editor: a System tab on the same page mirrors mymatasan's system panel -- running build/version info and live API/liveness/readiness health, refreshable on demand, alongside the restart control; a cache-provider dropdown reveals a Redis card with a live Test connection button (POST /api/settings/cache/test) that pings Redis with the in-progress form values (blank password falls back to the stored one) before anything is saved; every filesystem-path field (TLS cert/key, SSO CA cert, file-storage folder, log file) gets a Browse... button backed by a new whitelisted, read-only server-side file/folder picker (GET /api/settings/fs/browse, ported from mymatasan, confined to the working dir/data dir/home/common install locations); the Redis database number is a dropdown and fields with canonical values (default ports, multicast address, session-TTL presets, /metrics, callback path, localhost:6379) offer one-click autocomplete suggestions; and every field carries a plain-language (i) tooltip. The Save button is disabled until the section's working copy actually differs from what was loaded, with an inline "unsaved changes" indicator while dirty. Every save/reset (section name only, never values) and the /api/settings and /api/system routes themselves are recorded to the existing audit trail and endpoint catalog, matching the pattern used by the recent Reports feature.
compatibility: Purely additive: one new superadmin-only nav item/page, six new endpoints (GET /api/settings, GET/PUT /api/settings/{section}, POST /api/settings/{section}/reset, POST /api/settings/cache/test, GET /api/settings/fs/browse) plus POST /api/system/restart, all gated by existing session auth + an in-handler superadmin check -- no change to any existing endpoint, config default, or stored data. The Redis connectivity test and the filesystem browser are both read-only/non-persisting -- neither can write a file, read file contents, or change the live config, and a failed or cancelled test/browse leaves settings untouched. No schema/migration changes (reuses the existing ControlSetting key-value table for the first-run defaults snapshot). An existing install gains the page on upgrade with nothing to configure; editing a setting still requires an explicit restart (via the new in-app button or a normal process restart) before it takes effect, exactly as a manual config.json edit always has.
